data: {"type":"agent_chunk","agent":"synthesizer","content":"## How CRISPR Works

CRISPR gene editing is a genetic engineering technique for modifying the genomes of living organisms. It is based on a simplified version of the bacterial CRISPR-Cas9 antiviral defense system [1]. Cas9 nuclease is delivered into a cell with a synthetic guide RNA (gRNA), which allows the genome to be cut at a desired location [1]. In bacteria, CRISPR sequences are derived from bacteriophage DNA and are used to detect and destroy similar phage DNA during later infections [2].

## Types of Edits

Gene editing makes targeted DNA changes through insertion, deletion, or substitution. CRISPR, zinc finger nucleases, and TALENs are examples of tools that do this [3].

## Reported Applications

Headlines describe CRISPR as a possible treatment for a broad range of diseases [4]. Other headlines report that HIV in cell culture was eliminated using CRISPR-Cas editing [5]. Only the headlines were reviewed, so these claims are unconfirmed. The HIV result applies to cell culture, not to patients.

## Gaps and Limits

- The disease-treatment and HIV claims rest on headlines alone. The primary studies need to be located and read before these uses can be accepted.
- The mechanism summary omits off-target cutting, the main safety concern for any therapeutic use.
- The cited sources date from 2021 and 2024. Evidence published since then has not been checked.

### Sources

1. [CRISPR gene editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRISPR_gene_editing) - Wikipedia
2. [CRISPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRISPR) - Wikipedia
3. [Gene editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_editing) - Wikipedia
4. [CRISPR gene-editing breakthrough opens door to treating broad array of diseases](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=27643517) - Hacker News, 600 points, 234 comments, Jun 2021
5. [HIV in cell culture can be completely eliminated using CRISPR-Cas gene editing (pdf)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39761283) - Hacker News, 324 points, 77 comments, Mar 2024
